acceptance-criteria.criterion: When tags are posted to an existing link, the system shall attach them and return 200 with the link reporting every attached tag.
When a tag already attached to a link is posted again, the system shall return 200 and leave the tag attached exactly once.
If tags are posted to a link id that does not exist, then the system shall return 404 and create no tag rows.

context.data-model: Tag(id integer pk, name text unique not null) LinkTag(link_id fk Link.id, tag_id fk Tag.id, primary key both)

gaps.gap: Whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept is undecided. Keeping them makes an autocomplete list easy and lets the list rot.

context.prd-excerpt:
Feature "Tag links" (tag-links, should-have): Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column. This is the one place the fixture deliberately requires a real relationship: a single-table shortcut would make the data-model layer trivial and the fixture would stop exercising the part of layer planning most likely to break.
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable.
Considerations: Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct. This is an implementation constraint carried from the feature's notes/considerations block; it is NOT an acceptance criterion and has no id. Do not give it one.
Criterion tag-links#3, the tag filter on the listing endpoint, is NOT this task's. It was implemented in task L3-004 inside the single GET /links handler. Do not add a listing or filtering route here.
The gap carried in the gaps block above is tag-links gap 1, kind=decision, raised 2026-08-27, blocking=true. It is carried verbatim and UNANSWERED. layer_plan.json marks this gap as blocking and lists this task and L4-003 as affected, so this task should not be executed until the gap is answered. It does not, however, leak into this endpoint's surface: no detach endpoint, no cleanup endpoint, no cascade rule and no retention field is in scope here, and this task must not invent one to close the gap.

task.objective: Add a POST /links/{link_id}/tags handler to app/api/links.py that attaches one or more free-text tags to an existing link and returns 200 with the link reporting every tag attached to it, leaves an already-attached tag attached exactly once when it is posted again, and returns 404 without creating any tag rows when the link id does not exist.

requirements.requirement: Modify `app/api/links.py`. Do not create a new module and do not modify `app/main.py`. Add the handler to the existing `router` object; leave the existing POST /links and GET /links handlers unchanged.

Add these imports to `app/api/links.py`, keeping the ones already present:
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException from sqlalchemy import select from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.db import get_db from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag from app.schemas.tag import LinkWithTags, TagAttach

First statement of the handler body: look the link up and return 404 before touching Tag or LinkTag at all.
link = db.get(Link, link_id) if link is None: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Link not found")
Nothing may be added to the session before this check. Criterion 4 requires that a post to a missing link id creates no tag rows, and a Tag added to the session before the check can be flushed by a later query in the same request.

For each name in `payload.tags`, in the order supplied, find or create the Tag by exact name:
tag = db.scalars(select(Tag).where(Tag.name == name)).first() if tag is None: tag = Tag(name=name) db.add(tag) db.flush() # assigns tag.id without ending the transaction
`Tag.name == name` is an exact, case-sensitive comparison. Do not apply `lower()`, `ilike`, `collate("NOCASE")`, `strip()` or any other normalisation. Carried from the tag-links notes/considerations block ("Tag names are matched case-sensitively") as an implementation constraint, not as an acceptance criterion. "Python" and "python" are therefore two distinct tags.

Attach each tag only if it is not already attached:
existing = db.get(LinkTag, {"link_id": link.id, "tag_id": tag.id}) if existing is None: db.add(LinkTag(link_id=link.id, tag_id=tag.id)) db.flush()
Check for the existing row rather than catching IntegrityError. The composite primary key would raise on a duplicate insert, and an IntegrityError inside the request would abort the transaction and lose the rest of the payload. This check is what makes a repeat post return 200 with the tag attached exactly once, per criterion 2. The same check also makes a payload that repeats a name within one request attach it once.

Commit once, after the whole payload has been processed:
db.commit() db.refresh(link)

Build and return the response by reading back every tag currently attached to the link:
names = list( db.scalars( select(Tag.name) .join(LinkTag, LinkTag.tag_id == Tag.id) .where(LinkTag.link_id == link.id) .order_by(Tag.name.asc()) ).all() ) return LinkWithTags( id=link.id, url=link.url, title=link.title, created_at=link.created_at, tags=names, )
Read the names back from the database rather than echoing `payload.tags`, because criterion 1 requires the response to report EVERY attached tag, including tags attached by an earlier request.
Tag names are returned sorted ascending by name. This ordering is not specified by any criterion; it is chosen here so the response is deterministic and testable. SQLite's default TEXT collation is by code point, so uppercase names sort before lowercase ones.

Add no detach route, no tag-deletion route, no cleanup of orphaned tags and no cascade rule. Whether an orphaned tag is deleted or kept is the unanswered blocking gap tag-links gap 1, and implementing either behaviour here would silently answer it.
Do not add a listing or filtering route. The tag filter (criterion tag-links#3) already exists on the GET /links handler added by task L3-004.

test-requirements.test:
Create test file: `tests/test_tag_links.py`
Module imports:
import pytest from datetime import datetime from sqlalchemy import func, select from app.models.link import Link from app.models.link_tag import LinkTag from app.models.tag import Tag
Every test below takes the `client` and `db_session` fixtures from tests/conftest.py.
Shared setup used by tests 2 and 3, written inline in each test rather than as a fixture, so that this file adds no fixture of its own: link = Link(url="https://example.com/a", title="A", created_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, 0)) db_session.add(link) db_session.commit()

Test: test_posting_tags_to_an_existing_link_attaches_them_and_reports_every_tag Pattern is `event-driven`: one action, posting tags, produces one observable outcome, a 200 carrying the link with every attached tag. - Create the link as described in test 1. - response = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["python", "web"]}) - Assert response.status_code == 200 - body = response.json() - Assert body["id"] == link.id - Assert body["url"] == "https://example.com/a" - Assert body["title"] == "A" - Assert body["created_at"].startswith("2026-01-01T12:00:00") - Assert body["tags"] == ["python", "web"], sorted ascending by name. - Assert db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Tag)) == 2 - Assert db_session.scalar( select(func.count()).select_from(LinkTag).where(LinkTag.link_id == link.id) ) == 2 - Post a third tag in a second request: second = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["reading"]}) Assert second.status_code == 200 Assert second.json()["tags"] == ["python", "reading", "web"] This is the "EVERY attached tag" half of the criterion: the response reports the tag attached by the earlier request too, not only the one just posted.

Test: test_reposting_an_attached_tag_leaves_it_attached_exactly_once Pattern is `event-driven`: one action, reposting an attached tag, produces one observable outcome, a 200 with the tag still attached exactly once. - Create the link as described in test 1. - first = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["python"]}) Assert first.status_code == 200 and first.json()["tags"] == ["python"] - second = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["python"]}) Assert second.status_code == 200 Assert second.json()["tags"] == ["python"], the name appears once, not twice. - Assert db_session.scalar( select(func.count()).select_from(LinkTag).where(LinkTag.link_id == link.id) ) == 1 - Assert db_session.scalar( select(func.count()).select_from(Tag).where(Tag.name == "python") ) == 1 - Post a payload that repeats a name within one request: third = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["web", "web"]}) Assert third.status_code == 200 Assert third.json()["tags"] == ["python", "web"] Assert db_session.scalar( select(func.count()).select_from(LinkTag).where(LinkTag.link_id == link.id) ) == 2 - Additional assertion for the case-sensitivity constraint carried from the tag-links notes/considerations block, not for the criterion: fourth = client.post(f"/links/{link.id}/tags", json={"tags": ["Python"]}) Assert fourth.status_code == 200 Assert fourth.json()["tags"] == ["Python", "python", "web"], so "Python" is a new tag rather than a repost of "python", and uppercase sorts first under code-point ordering. Assert db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Tag)) == 3

Test: test_posting_tags_to_a_missing_link_returns_404_and_creates_no_tag_rows Pattern is `unwanted-behaviour`, so assert the error path: the thing that must not happen, tag rows created for a link that does not exist, does not happen. - Do NOT create any link. Confirm the id is absent: Assert db_session.get(Link, 999999) is None - response = client.post("/links/999999/tags", json={"tags": ["python", "web"]}) - Assert response.status_code == 404 - Assert response.json() == {"detail": "Link not found"} - Assert db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Tag)) == 0 - Assert db_session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(LinkTag)) == 0 These two counts are the "create no tag rows" half of the criterion, and they are the reason requirement 4 puts the lookup before any session write.

exports.interface:
POST /links/{link_id}/tags
Path parameters: link_id: int, the id of an existing link.
Request body: application/json {"tags": ["python", "web"]} At least one name is required. Names are free text and are matched case-sensitively: "Python" and "python" are two distinct tags. Names are not stripped or normalised.
Response 200: application/json, a LinkWithTags object reporting the link and EVERY tag currently attached to it, including tags attached by earlier requests. Tag names are sorted ascending by name.
{ "id": 7, "url": "https://example.com/a", "title": "A", "created_at": "2026-01-01T12:00:00", "tags": ["python", "web"] }
"title" is null rather than omitted when the link has no title. Reposting an already-attached tag returns 200 and leaves it attached exactly once.
Response 404: application/json, {"detail": "Link not found"} Returned when link_id does not exist. No Tag and no LinkTag row is created.
Response 422: returned by FastAPI when the body has no tags key or an empty tags list.
No detach route and no tag-cleanup route exists: the orphaned-tag decision is the unanswered blocking gap tag-links gap 1.
